hints: Start by drawing out 2-methylbut-1-ene and look closely at what is attached to each carbon of the C=C double bond.
Notice that C-1 has two identical H atoms, so swapping groups cannot give a different cis-trans arrangement.
Think Markovnikov for HBr addition, H goes to the carbon already with more H and Br goes to the more substituted carbon, then check which bromoalkane that really gives.
walkthrough:
**Draw the alkene structure**

First, let us see what we are working with. 2-methylbut-1-ene is an alkene with the double bond at C-1.

Chemical structure:
$$\text{CH}_2 = \text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Test Student 1, geometrical isomerism**

For cis-trans (E/Z) isomerism, each C of the C=C must have two different groups attached. Restricted rotation alone is not enough.

Here, C-1 is $\text{CH}_2$ with two identical H atoms, while C-2 has $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Because one end has identical groups, no geometrical isomers are possible. So Student 1 is wrong.

**Test Student 2, addition of HBr**

Alkenes undergo electrophilic addition with HBr. The major product follows Markovnikov's rule: H adds to the C with more H atoms, Br adds to the more substituted carbocation.

Rule in words:
$$\text{H to C with most H, Br to most stable carbocation}$$

**Find the real major product**

H adds to C-1 ($\text{CH}_2$) to give a tertiary carbocation at C-2, then $\text{Br}^-$ attacks there.

Correct major product:
$$\text{CH}_2 = \text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CBr}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
That is 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, not 1-bromo-2-methylbutane. So Student 2 is also wrong, and neither student is correct.

options.A: Incorrect, as both statements fail. C-1 has two H atoms so no geometrical isomerism exists, and Markovnikov addition gives 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, not the 1-bromo isomer.
options.B: Incorrect. Student 1 is wrong because 2-methylbut-1-ene is $\text{CH}_2 = \text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The $\text{CH}_2$ end has two identical substituents, which is a classic trap for assuming any substituted alkene shows cis-trans isomerism.
options.C: Incorrect. Student 2 is wrong because it reverses Markovnikov's rule. H adds to C-1 to form the more stable tertiary carbocation at C-2, so Br ends up on C-2 to give 2-bromo-2-methylbutane as the main product.
options.D: Correct. Student 1 is wrong (no E/Z isomerism due to two H on C-1) and Student 2 is wrong (Markovnikov product is 2-bromo-2-methylbutane). Therefore neither student is correct.
